references.text: In Leviticus 12:6-8 it is described that a woman who has given birth shall bring an offering to the priest: a year-old lamb as a burnt offering and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering. If she cannot afford a lamb, she may bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a burnt offering and the other as a sin offering. This refers to the law of purification after childbirth, which Mary followed in Luke 2:24.

In Exodus 13:2 it is commanded that all firstborn, both of humans and animals, belong to the Lord. This underscores the importance of the ritual Mary performs in Luke 2:24, by offering for her firstborn son in accordance with the law.
